title: Sent to Build Bridges, He Spent His Life Painting Them
standfirst: In 1886 Theodor Pallady's family enrolled him in Bucharest's school for civil engineers. He quit within a year for an art studio in Dresden and never went back — though decades later, in Paris, a bag of embroidered blouses he handed a friend named Henri Matisse became one of the more famous paintings of the century.

sections.heading: He Was Enrolled to Build Actual Bridges Before He Painted Any
sections.body: In 1886 Theodor Pallady enrolled in Bucharest's [School of Bridges and Roads](https://www.rador.ro/2021/04/09/theodor-pallady-150-de-ani-de-la-nastere/), the institution that trained the country's civil engineers, because that was the profession his parents wanted for their son. He had been born fifteen years earlier in Iași to Ioan Pallady and Maria Cantacuzino, sister of the diplomat Neculai B. Cantacuzino. The engineering plan barely survived a year. By 1887 he had switched to the Dresden Polytechnic, still nominally studying the same subject, while taking private lessons on the side from the landscape painter Erwin Oehme. It was Oehme who told him to stop treating painting as the side project and go to Paris instead.

sections.heading: Gustave Moreau's Studio Put Him Beside Matisse for Life
sections.body: Pallady reached Paris in 1889 and spent several years moving between teachers — Edmond Aman-Jean, the classes of Puvis de Chavannes, spells with Aimé Morot and Fernand Cormon — before joining [Gustave Moreau's studio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Theodor_Pallady) in 1892. Moreau's students that year also included Henri Matisse, Georges Rouault and Albert Marquet. Of that group, Pallady and Matisse [became close friends](https://ambogdan.com/la-blouse-roumaine-henri-matisse/), and the friendship held for the rest of both men's lives — long after Matisse's palette had become the loudest in twentieth-century painting and Pallady's had stayed deliberately, stubbornly quiet.

sections.heading: He Gave Matisse a Bag of Blouses. Matisse Spent Six Years on Them.
sections.body: At some point in their long friendship, Pallady gave Matisse a set of embroidered Romanian peasant blouses. Matisse put them away among his studio props and, according to his assistant Lydia Delectorskaya, [rediscovered them in 1937](https://www.sothebys.com/en/auctions/ecatalogue/2014/impressionist-modern-art-evening-sale-l14002/lot.45.html), by which point he and Pallady were corresponding regularly about art. Their geometric embroidery became the anchor of a run of paintings and drawings that reached [ten versions between 1939 and 1945](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La_Blouse_Roumaine). The last and best known of them, La Blouse Roumaine, took [six months of work](https://www.centrepompidou.fr/en/pompidou-plus/magazine/article/focus-on-la-blouse-roumaine-by-henri-matisse) and was finished in April 1940; it now hangs at the Centre Pompidou. Pallady's own name barely survives in most accounts of the picture. His blouses are the reason it exists.

sections.heading: Critics Filed Him Under "Style's Own Conscience"
sections.body: Romanian criticism settled on an epithet for Pallady that recurs across his obituaries and anniversaries: ["pictorul conştiinţei stilului"](https://www.rador.ro/2021/04/11/portret-theodor-pallady-pictorul-constiintei-stilului-150-de-ani-de-la-nastere/), the painter of style's own conscience — praise for a man specialists still class jointly as an Impressionist and Post-Impressionist rather than settle on one label. WikiArt files this canvas simply as Impressionism, with no year attached to it at all. Pallady's own output leaned toward restraint rather than the movement's loose, weather-chasing brushwork: still lifes, interiors, and the [Parisian views](https://romfilatelia.ro/en/theodor-pallady-the-150th-anniversary-of-his-birth/) — Seine bridges, street corners, the flowers outside his Place Dauphine studio — that critics have since compared more to Albert Marquet and Pierre Bonnard than to Monet or Pissarro. One retrospective description called his temperament a rational spirit of measure, avoiding exaggeration in either direction.

sections.heading: He Left Place Dauphine the Same Year Matisse Finished the Blouse
sections.body: Pallady kept his Paris studio on Place Dauphine until 1940, when the war forced him back to Bucharest for good — the same year, as it happens, that Matisse finished La Blouse Roumaine three thousand kilometres away. Pallady kept working into his eighties; a [1956 retrospective](https://romfilatelia.ro/en/theodor-pallady-the-150th-anniversary-of-his-birth/) mounted while he was still alive filled Bucharest's Art Museum with 202 paintings and 87 works on paper, and that same year the state named him Master Emeritus of Art. He died on 16 August 1956 and was buried at Bellu Cemetery; the Romanian Academy admitted him as a member only after his death. Most of what survives from his Paris decades — some [800 drawings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Theodor_Pallady_Museum) — now hangs in Casa Melik, a Bucharest merchant's house built in the second half of the eighteenth century and named for an entirely different man, the merchant Iacob Melic. It has carried Pallady's name only since it became his museum.
